Thanks Aisha — useful start. A couple of clarifying questions from Acme Legal and procurement:

1) Residency question: your doc mentions ‘data may be processed in other jurisdictions’. We need a short line confirming whether customer data will ever be routed to China/HK (this is a red flag for our procurement).
2) Subprocessors: can you confirm whether any caching or CDN providers are considered subprocessors (we need to list all subprocessors that persist data).
3) Retention: your snippet says ‘temporary caching to speed up responses’ — we need a two-sentence description that makes clear how long cached tokens are kept and whether they are accessible to support teams.

Finally, procurement would like a 1-sentence public blurb for our external-facing procurement page and a 1-2 sentence tooltip for your console Data Residency toggle (non-legal, understandable by ops folks). If you could send those separately that’d make approvals faster.

Cc’d Acme Legal for their redlines.

—Devon

Subject: Re: Hosted API privacy — short public summaries & procurement blurb

Hi Devon — great questions. Quick internal note followed by proposed snippets below. Attaching an updated summary and a subprocessor CSV for visibility (subprocessor-map_oct2026.csv).

Internal: Kimberly, Rishi — please confirm the factual parts below (China routing, cache retention policy, support access).

Proposed public-facing 1-sentence procurement blurb (for Acme site):
"Redwood Inference processes requests on behalf of customers and uses a limited set of subprocessors for infrastructure and monitoring; we do not use subprocessors that retain customer content for product development without your consent."

Proposed console tooltip (2 sentences, non-legal):
"Data residency controls where requests are processed. Choosing a region keeps processing in that geographic area when possible; in rare cases we may route requests to a nearby region for reliability or capacity."

Responses to Devon's questions (draft):
- China/HK routing: We do not route customer request payloads to Mainland China or Hong Kong for hosted API processing by default. If a customer requires on-prem or a local region deployment, we support Private deployments (we can add this sentence to the Blurb).
- Caching/CDN: Persistent caches and object stores used in the runtime (e.g., Redis clusters) that store request-derived tokens are considered subprocessors; ephemeral local caches on GPU nodes are not treated as persistent subprocessors. A CSV of current subprocessors is attached.
- Retention: Short-lived KV/prefix caches are kept <1 hour by default; any persisted logs used for debugging are retained up to 30 days and are accessible to support under strict audit controls.

Attachment: subprocessor-map_oct2026.csv, public-snippets_v2.txt

Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API privacy — short public summaries & procurement blurb

Thanks Laura — small edits below and a tightened set of snippets (see inline). I moved the residency sentence to be clearer and removed the phrase ‘may be processed in other jurisdictions’ because it felt ambiguous. Also replaced ‘support access’ with ‘access under documented support procedures’ to reduce misunderstandings.

Final suggested 1-sentence procurement blurb:
"Redwood Inference processes customer requests and uses a limited set of subprocessors for infrastructure and monitoring; we do not use subprocessors to retain customer content for product development without explicit customer agreement."

Final console tooltip (non-technical, two sentences):
"Data residency determines the preferred geographic location where requests are processed. When a residency is selected we try to keep processing in that region; in rare cases we may route to a nearby region to maintain service availability."

Cache/retention clarification to include in the DPA summary:
"Short-lived in-memory caches (used to accelerate responses) are retained for under one hour; persistent logs kept for debugging are retained up to 30 days and are only accessible to support engineers via audited procedures. External CDN providers that persist request content are listed as subprocessors in our public subprocessor map."

I’ve attached a cleaned text file (public-snippets_v2.txt) with these lines so you can drop them into your procurement page or the console tooltip. If Acme Legal wants any additional precision (e.g., exact list of CDN providers), we can provide a signed addendum.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
